text:
Leah: hey team, new hire question. I can connect to WireGuard, assigned 10.4.7.21, but I can't reach any IPv4-only internal services (10.4.x.x). `ssh -J bastionsvc@bastion.redwood 10.4.8.12` works, but direct curl to 10.4 addresses from my laptop times out. I recently switched to a new ISP that advertised IPv6-only home networks. anyone run into IPv6-only client + split-tunnel issues?
Hana: welcome! yes, IPv6-only ISPs can surface odd behavior. can you paste `wg show`, `ip a`, and `curl -v --ipv4 http://10.4.8.12:8080` vs `curl -v --ipv6 http://[...]:8080` (if you have an IPv6 mapped address)?
Leah: paste below:
```
$ wg show
interface: wg-redwood
  assigned ip: 10.4.7.21/32
  peer: AAAA...bbb
    allowed ips: 10.4.0.0/16, 172.19.0.0/16
$ ip -6 addr show scope global
2: eth0: <...> inet6 2601:abcd:123::5/64 scope global
$ ip route show
default via fe80::1 dev eth0 proto ra metric 1024
10.4.0.0/16 dev wg-redwood scope link
```
Leah: `curl -4 -v http://10.4.8.12:8080` hangs. `curl -6 -v http://[2604:internal::8]:8080` not applicable because internal infra is v4-only.
netops-bot: Note: Assigned client IPv4 10.4.7.21, policy split-tunnel. Detected host has global IPv6 (2601:...) and kernel prefers IPv6 for outgoing lookups. Internal services are IPv4-only.
Omar: likely the kernel chooses an IPv6 source or DNS returns IPv6 AAAA for some public endpoints and the system prefers v6 sockets. But since internal IPs are v4-only, the problem might be that your host's IPv4 traffic is being NAT64-translated by the ISP (if provided) or dropped because the host's IPv4 stack isn't routing via wg-redwood. can you run `sudo ip -4 route get 10.4.8.12` and `sysctl net.ipv4.conf.all.route_localnet`?
Leah: `ip -4 route get 10.4.8.12` shows `via 192.168.100.1 dev eth0` (my local gateway) which is surprising because wg has route for 10.4/16.
Hana: aha that means the OS didn't install the expected route precedence for IPv4 due to the way your ISP's RA config interacts with netstack. Two quick workarounds to get you unblocked: (A) disable IPv6 temporarily so IPv4 route selection behaves normally: `sudo sysctl -w net.ipv6.conf.all.disable_ipv6=1` (B) force source-based routing so packets from your 10.4.7.21 go out via wg-redwood table:
```
sudo ip rule add from 10.4.7.21/32 table 220
sudo ip route add default dev wg-redwood table 220
```
Omar: alternative short-term: use SSH SOCKS through bastion `ssh -D1080 bastionsvc@bastion.redwood` and point your browser/cli to socks5://localhost:1080. That avoids kernel routing weirdness.
Leah: I tried disabling IPv6 and `curl http://10.4.8.12:8080` immediately worked. The ip rule solution also worked but I had to be careful to persist it across reboots.
IT-ops: for onboarding we tag clients with `wg-ipv4-route-fix` when we detect global IPv6 but need consistent IPv4 split-tunnel behavior (ticket ONB-5601). We can reprovision your profile to include the source-based route or push an OS-specific helper script. If you want, DM your onboarding ticket and we'll add the tag.
Leah: thanks! I opened ONB-5601 and requested `wg-ipv4-route-fix`. One follow-up: is disabling IPv6 safe long-term?
Hana: disabling IPv6 is only a temporary workaround. We prefer the source-based routing approach or provisioning a small user-level script that runs at login. Also security/monitoring teams prefer not to force-disable IPv6 broadly. We'll add the routing fix to your profile instead.
Leah: great, marking resolved for now. thanks for the quick help and welcome :wave:
